summary: A response from Peggy Karp of MITRE to a request for comments on computer-based instruction over the network. She attaches excerpts from an internal MITRE status report describing the company's ARPANET studies. These cover how MITRE joined the network through a terminal IMP in 1971 and how it planned to use network resources, including instructional ones.

plainLanguage.summary: MITRE reported on experiments to use ARPANET computers and programs to extend its TICCIT teaching system. Some remote tools had been tried, while other connections and storage work remained in progress.

subtitle: MITRE's report on using network resources for instruction

tldr.problem: MITRE wanted to investigate whether remote network resources could extend the TICCIT computer-assisted instruction system.
tldr.mechanism: Its plans included remote graphics, computer-assisted instruction systems such as SCHOLAR and LOGO, and network storage and computing resources.
tldr.outcome: The report describes progress and limitations, including successful use of SCHOLAR and ongoing work to connect graphics systems.

today: RFC 321 is a progress report on MITRE's computer-based instruction studies. It distinguishes work already tried from plans and tasks that had not yet begun.

sections.title: MITRE's Network Study
sections.content:
This report responds to a request for comments about computer-based instruction. MITRE describes three aims for its network study: use network resources in its own work, conduct experiments in sharing data, and test whether remote resources could add capabilities to TICCIT, its computer-assisted instruction system.

The report says MITRE joined the ARPANET in September 1971 through a TIP.
sections.plainLanguage: MITRE used the network to study how distant computers could support its teaching system. The report separates this work into network use, data sharing and teaching-system experiments.

sections.title: Remote Graphics and Teaching Programs
sections.content:
MITRE planned to use the Culler-Fried graphics system at UCSB for mathematics instruction and to explore computer science courses using network systems. It also selected SCHOLAR and LOGO as possible additions to TICCIT. SCHOLAR had been used over the network with a geography database, while the report describes plans to test LOGO and its display turtle.

Graphics output required additional work to map it to the IMLAC display at MITRE.
sections.plainLanguage: MITRE tried a remote teaching program and planned to connect a graphics system for mathematics. It also wanted to test LOGO, but graphics connections still needed work.

sections.title: Limits and Next Steps
sections.content: The report says many network resources had been built as standalone systems, so using them remotely took more work than expected. MITRE planned to demonstrate selected systems over the network but would not interconnect the systems during fiscal year 1972. It also describes proposed work to use remote storage for curriculum material and student records, and another host for statistical analysis; that subtask had not begun.
sections.plainLanguage: Remote systems were not designed to connect easily, so MITRE planned demonstrations rather than a fully joined teaching system that year. The storage and analysis work had not started.
